# Privacy filter test pictures

Both pictures are photographs by NASA, a United States government agency, and are in the **public domain** in the
United States (works of the US federal government, 17 U.S.C. § 105). They were downloaded on 2026-11-22 as the
1280-pixel-wide renditions Wikimedia Commons serves, and are used unchanged.

| File | Shows | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `crew.jpg` | Six people facing the camera (the Expedition 49 crew portrait) | https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Expedition_49_crew_portrait_(2).jpg |
| `control.jpg` | Flight controllers seen from behind, wall screens and console monitors (Mission Control, Apollo 14 splashdown, NASA S71-18400) | https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Flight_Controllers_in_Mission_Control_Center_during_splashdown_of_Apollo_14_(S71-18400).jpg |

Why these: the filter must be tested on real faces, real people seen from behind and real screens, not on a synthetic
camera with no faces. Public-domain pictures of people who were photographed for publication avoid using anyone's
likeness without consent. QR codes, phone numbers and the test video are generated by the tests from these pictures.

They replace the frame of Offleak's demo clip that the first browser test read from the extracted upstream folder,
which is no longer needed.
